title: Kremlin Prepares to Cross the Final Red Line
content:
After the first wave of compulsory mobilization in 2022 brought broad opposition and an exodus of young men, the Russian authorities did their homework. As a result, they are significantly better prepared for the next round, which many observers expect may follow the September 18-20 Duma elections.

But surveys carried out by the Kyiv-based Institute for Conflict Studies and Analysis of Russia show opposition is not just high, it is also increasing.

Many Russians are deeply unhappy at the idea, and Putin’s inner circle, despite its tight control of information and communications, will have to take their opposition into account. Finding ways out of the country for their fighting age children has become an urgent talking point among middle class Russians in Moscow and St Petersburg.

Negative attitudes to compulsory mobilization became entrenched after the first wave, in the fall of 2022, and the share of Russians opposed to a repeat has remained at around three-quarters of the population since early 2024.

title: ‘Horror in the sky’: Ukraine races for a solution to Russian jet-powered drones
content:
KYIV — Russia is upgrading its attack drones by powering them with fast turbojet engines, making them much more difficult to intercept and forcing Ukraine to develop technology to knock them down.

The shift is adding to the strain on a country already accustomed to nights spent under air-raid alerts: faster drones give air-defense crews less time to respond, can outpace the defenses that helped counter earlier Shaheds and threaten homes, transport and critical infrastructure across Ukraine.

“Together with dozens of Ukrainian companies, we are already looking for cheap and mass-produced solutions, in particular for intercepting jet-powered drones. Some interceptors are already undergoing combat testing,” Ukrainian Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara said last week at a meeting of Ukraine’s allies.

“We cannot simply wait while Russia refines its repertoire of killings. Right now, we need to focus as much attention as possible on securing the skies, finding ways to protect people, and scaling up our response to Russian drones,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last Friday.

title: Two Khuzestan Residents Arrested, Two Musicians Summoned Over Song
content:
According to HRANA, on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, Mehdi Naseri was arrested by IRGC Intelligence agents in Ahvaz.

According to information received by HRANA, Naseri’s arrest was related to his cultural activities and the production and release of a song titled “From Karun to Olive” (“Az Karun ta Zeytun”).

A source familiar with the matter told HRANA that the work had previously received official authorization; however, its video was removed from online platforms after being released.

Subsequently, on Saturday, September 12, Aref Naseri, Mehdi Naseri’s cousin, was arrested by IRGC Intelligence agents in the Saadi district of Shadegan. Security forces also searched his home during the arrest.

Aref Naseri, also known as “Abu Nayef,” is a poet and host of a cultural program published online.

At the same time, Hossein Ahvazi and Mehdi Zaeri, two musicians who collaborated on the production of “From Karun to Olive,” were summoned by IRGC Intelligence. According to information received by HRANA, the summonses were also related to the production and release of the same work.

title: Two Shot, Several Arrested in Clashes Over Papua New Guinea Mine
content:
At least two people were shot and several arrested in the Papua New Guinea island of Bougainville on Sunday after unknown people set fire to equipment belonging to an Indian company poised to reopen one of the world’s largest untapped copper and gold reserves.

The arson attack targeted a mining camp belonging to Lloyds Metals and Energy Ltd, an Indian company that was controversially chosen by Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama to reopen the long-shuttered Panguna mine, which is estimated to hold $160 billion in precious metals.

The attack, which sparked a shootout and retaliation, came three weeks after an OCCRP investigation raised questions about Toroama’s decision to choose Lloyds.

The investigation revealed that Toroama had signed a memorandum of understanding with Lloyds shortly after accepting an offer from its managing director for the president’s wife to travel to India and have a life-saving kidney operation at no cost.

It also quoted an expert and some locals warning that anger over the Indian company’s involvement could erupt into violence.

title: Sweden elections: why immigrants are underrepresented at the polls
content:
The Swedish election has turned into a nail-biter. With the majority of votes counted in the contest for the national parliament, only a few tenths of a percentage point separate the left-leaning opposition “red-green” bloc and the incumbent centre-right coalition. This group is commonly known as the “Tidö” bloc.

The opposition Social Democrats, led by former Swedish prime minister Magdalena Andersson, has emerged as the largest group in parliament. Preliminary results suggest it has won around 100 seats out of 349. This is its lowest share of the vote in more than a century.

But as smaller left-leaning parties improved their positions compared with elections in 2022, the “red-greens” collectively would have a small majority if the final results confirm the preliminary picture. There are ideological differences between the parties of the left, so it is not a foregone conclusion that Andersson will be able to form a viable government.

title: Physicists zoom into the birth of cosmic rainstorms with new CERN study
content:
Every second, particles zip through your body at nearly the speed of light. They rain down from a storm high in the sky, where cosmic rays, a powerful type of interstellar matter, are constantly striking atoms in Earth’s atmosphere. The impacts break them apart into a shower of particles that rain to the ground.

Scientists have studied these cosmic rainstorms for over a century, but they lack a precise understanding of how they form. Many researchers are searching for a clearer picture, and they don’t even need to look to the sky to study them. They can instead use a particle collider, CERN’s Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland.

With a team of particle physicists, I study how these cosmic rainstorms are born. We used the world’s first laboratory collisions of oxygen atoms with protons to simulate cosmic rays in the lab. Our results are now published in Physical Review Letters.

In the early 20th century, physicist Victor Hess discovered cosmic rays aboard hot air balloons. While ascending several kilometers, his instruments found radiation levels unexpectedly kept rising. He deduced these rays must come from space and received the 1936 Nobel Prize in physics for this discovery.

title: Nimet paperiin: Suomi ja Ranska ovat nyt ”strategisia kumppaneita”
content:
Suomen ja Ranskan ulkoministerit Elina Valtonen (kok.) ja Jean-Noël Barrot allekirjoittivat maanantaina Helsingissä asiakirjan maiden strategisesta kumppanuudesta.

Maiden välillä sovittuun kokonaisuuteen kuului muun muassa Suomen liittyminen Ranskan ydinpelotealoitteeseen eli niin kutsuttuun eteenpäin työnnettyyn pelotteeseen, mistä tiedotettiin jo aiemmin maanantaina.

Aloite ei tarkoita sitä, että Ranska ulottaisi ydinsateenvarjonsa myös Suomen ylle, ja sen konkreettinen merkitys jäikin vielä maanantaina avoimeksi. Alustavasti sen arveltiin tietävän ainakin lisääntyvää yhteistä harjoittelutoimintaa.

- Yhteistyö on vasta alussa. Kuva tarkentuu, kun puolustushallinto aloittaa keskustelut Ranskan kanssa yhteistyön etenemisestä, kertoi Valtonen ministerien yhteisessä lehdistötilaisuudessa.

- Strategisessa kumppanuudessa on kyse prosessista, jossa voidaan mennä eteenpäin, sanoi Barrot.

Barrot kertoi toimittajille, että strategista kumppanuutta tiivistetään myös esimerkiksi yhteiskunnan kestävyyden kehittämisessä ja nousevissa teknologioissa kuten tekoälyssä ja kvanttitietokoneissa.

title: Googlen miljardi-investointi Suomeen – vihreät peräänkuuluttavat kestävyyttä ja tiukempaa otetta
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Googlen ilmoitus miljardi-investoinnista Suomeen sijoittuviin datakeskuksiin herättää keskustelua myös vihreiden riveissä. Puolueen edustajat suhtautuvat uutiseen myönteisesti, mutta kritisoivat hallituksen toimintaa.

Vihreän eduskuntaryhmän puheenjohtaja Oras Tynkkynen pitää Googlen ennätysinvestointia kaivattuna ilouutisena Suomen taloudelle.

"Googlen ennätysinvestointi on kipeästi kaivattu ilouutinen Suomen taloudelle. Se myös vahvistaa alueiden elinvoimaa ja tuo sekä rakennusaikaisia että pysyviä työpaikkoja", Tynkkynen sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

Googlen julkistama paketti on arvioitu sekä Suomen suurimmaksi yksittäiseksi investoinniksi että yhtiön suurimmaksi panostukseksi Euroopassa. Tynkkysen mukaan tämä kertoo vihreän siirtymän vetovoimasta kansainvälisessä kilpailussa.

"Suomi pystyy jo nyt tarjoamaan 95-prosenttisesti fossiilisista polttoaineista putsatun sähköjärjestelmän ja kansainvälisessä vertailussa varsin hyvät edellytykset liittyä sähköverkkoon. Vihreys on yksi Suomen suurimpia valtteja kovassa kansainvälisessä kilpailussa investoinneista, eikä sitä ole varaa politiikalla tärvätä", Tynkkynen arvioi.

title: “We mostly do this stuff just for the love of it”: WikiCelebrating Juan “BugWarp” Kulichevsky
content:
We are proud to WikiCelebrate Juan Kulichevsky today, known across Wikimedia projects as User:BugWarp. Juan has contributed to Wikimedia projects since childhood and is passionate about sports photography, free knowledge, and community building in Argentina and beyond.

Juan’s Wikimedia journey began in a pretty unusual way when he was just 10 years old.

“It’s quite funny actually, if you look at my account, I’ve been registered since July 2009. I was only 10 years old then! Already back then we used Wikipedia a lot with my friends at school so we could finish our homework,” Juan remembers. Inspired after a friend’s father donated to Wikipedia, Juan decided the “coolest thing” he could do was create an account himself.

“Little did I know that this would be the start of something great. Many years later, I remembered that you can freely contribute to the project, and I started uploading pictures to Commons of people and things that weren’t available on Wiki, and then I took the courage to start editing and writing articles.” Juan says.

Today, much of his work focuses on sports photography and improving the visual representation of athletes across Wikimedia projects.

title: The Route to Cappyness review – capybara boosterism is an ode to the internet’s favourite rodent
content:
From a cappy-cafe owner in Japan to an escaped capybara in the UK, this homespun film takes the temperature of an international obsession

One of Midlands-based film-maker Sharon Walia’s previous works was The Keepers of the Pigs, proudly described on her production company’s website as “the first ever documentary about guinea pigs”. So it makes zoological sense that her latest film takes on capybaras, guinea pigs’ ridiculously cute semi-aquatic cousins that are indigenous to Latin America, and relatively recently became ubiquitous on social media in memes and short films alike. As glimpsed here, there was even a capybara in the recent Academy Award-winning animated feature Flow, some pro-cappy boosterism that captured the creatures’ chill vibe and snuffly sweetness.

Walia’s celebration of the species stays on script, rejoicing in the animals’ natural geniality, friendliness to other species in their natural habitat, and their compelling, remunerative charm that seems to have bolstered the fortunes of several animal attractions around the world.

title: Frontline Arctic: The Evolution of Russia’s Military Posture in a Changing Arctic
content:
• Russia’s military posture and regional threat perception are steadfast. They relate to imposing cost on the access of foreign military assets to the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation (AZRF) and through the Northern Sea Route (NSR); ensuring defense in depth by expanding interdiction capabilities beyond the AZRF; and protecting the NSR from perceived foreign encroachment against its disputable status as a “body of internal waters”.
  • Despite unchanging strategic priorities, the Kremlin has been compelled to adapt its military, defense, and security approach toward the region. These changes are compounded by over a decade of war against Ukraine, international isolation, sanctions, and the accelerating impacts of climate change. Russian authorities are vindicated but more vulnerable in the Arctic, a region where Moscow once held strategic dominance.
  • Moscow feels that both its control and sovereignty over the Arctic are slipping away. Russia is feeling increasingly vulnerable in the Arctic, especially in the context of Sweden and Finland joining NATO. Conventional limitations amplify the Kremlin’s increasing sense of vulnerability, particularly in the European High North.

title: Von der Leyen to skip Carney speech in EU Parliament
content:
STRASBOURG — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will not attend Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s address to the European Parliament on Thursday. 

Carney will speak to lawmakers on Thursday at 11.30 a.m. as he seeks closer ties with the EU amid deteriorating relations with Washington. He is expected to set out his wishlist for Brussels ahead of a Canada-EU summit in October. The address comes a day after he will attend von der Leyen’s annual State of the Union speech.

During Carney’s speech, the Commission will instead be represented by Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič — one of von der Leyen’s most trusted lieutenants — the executive’s chief spokesperson Paula Pinho confirmed.

The Commission president won’t be in Strasbourg on Thursday as she has to return to Brussels due to “prior commitments,” Pinho said. One of those prior commitments is a press conference on the child online safety initiative.

title: January 2026 Protests: Erfan Haj Bonyan Dehaghani Sentenced to Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Erfan Haj Bonyan Dehaghani has been sentenced to prison.

According to a ruling issued on August 11 by Branch 5 of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Vahid Hemmat-Nejad as an advisory judge, Haj Bonyan Dehaghani was sentenced to one year in prison on the charge of “propaganda activity against the regime through participation in the January 8 gatherings, wearing distinctive clothing bearing writings against national interests, and activity on social media.”

He was also sentenced to 10 years in prison on non-political charges brought against him in the same case. These charges were brought following a search of his home and were based on claims by IRGC Intelligence agents that he possessed prohibited items (six grams of hallucinogenic mushrooms).

During his arrest and the search of his home, security forces confiscated many of his personal and valuable belongings, including digital devices, clothing, cash, and cryptocurrency-related assets.

He was arrested on March 6, 2026, and was released on bail on April 7, 2026.

Erfan Haj Bonyan Dehaghani, aged approximately 26, works in cryptocurrency trading, and resides in Isfahan.

title: Inside ‘Project Lily’: The Humans Reading Your ChatGPT Chats
content:
OpenAI is hiring hundreds of contractors who read a massive stream of real users’ ChatGPT prompts, with the prompts sometimes including sensitive personal information, 404 Media has learned. The prompts these people review can include whole conversations between users and the chatbot, conversations that most of ChatGPT’s more than 900 million users probably don’t realize may be read by actual people.

The goal of these prompt review teams is to improve the responses ChatGPT gives to its users, with the contractors rating and critiquing the chatbot’s generated replies. Internal documents seen by 404 Media show contractors training ChatGPT to not anthropomorphize itself, and to be less sycophantic, a key problem for OpenAI whose over-sycophantic 4o model led in part to multiple peoples’ suicides, according to various lawsuits.

title: Philippine President's Cousin to be Transferred from Hospital to Jail
content:
The Philippines’ anti-graft court on Monday ordered the transfer of Martin Romualdez, former House Speaker and cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., from a hospital to a regular jail a week after his arrest, OCCRP partner Rappler reported. Romualdez is accused of plunder in a 7.44-billion-peso ($118 million) case.

The transfer order follows a medical report from the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) concluding that Romualdez is clinically stable and no longer requires hospitalization. He will be moved to the New Quezon City Jail, where he will be detained while hearings on his plunder charge are conducted.

Prosecutors allege that, between 2022 and 2025, Romualdez and his co-defendants amassed billions of pesos through commissions, kickbacks and bribes from contractors and other entities seeking government infrastructure work.

title: Is calisthenics as good as weight training? Here’s what the science says
content:
Calisthenics has gained enormous popularity in recent years, particularly thanks to social media and the rise of workout areas in city parks. You probably know some of the moves already, like pull-ups, push-ups, dips and squats.

For the more advanced, it also includes eye-catching, gravity-defying moves like the muscle-up, planche (where the body is held horizontal, supported solely by the hands) or the front lever (where the body is held horizontally while hanging from a bar).

But is calisthenics an effective form of exercise, or just another fitness fad? To answer this question, we first need to clarify what it is.

Calisthenics is a form of training that mainly uses a person’s own body weight as resistance. Its name derives from the Greek terms kállos (“beautiful”) and sthenos (“strength”), though the word’s modern use only caught on during the 19th century, when it referred to various forms of physical exercise.

title: Houthi rebels’ control of Red Sea oil chokepoint exposes deep divisions in Brics
content:
Houthi rebel forces have seized the Yemeni port of Mokha as well as Mayyun Island overlooking the Bab el-Mandab strait. This gives Iran’s most powerful remaining proxy force in the Middle East nearly complete control of Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast.

Directly or indirectly, Tehran now has a chokehold on around 12% of global trade that passes through that waterway. It is also maintaining its pressure on the Strait of Hormuz, which has already led to a cut of flows there from about 9 million barrels of oil a day to between 3.7 and 6.4 million.

The day after the Houthis took control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, Brics leaders assembled in New Delhi, for their 18th annual summit. Brics is the group of “emerging economies” which formed around Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa in 2006, to counter western influence in global institutions. It has since added six permanent members: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE and Indonesia. A further ten countries, Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam joined as “partner countries” in 2025.

content:
Three little letters - bnb-side’s name is a play on the local b-side arts festival, but Silicon Valley colossus sees threat to global brand

title: EU to limit access to social media before age of 15
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission will propose new rules to restrict minors’ access to social media and video-sharing platforms before the age of 15, according to preparatory documents seen by POLITICO and a person familiar with the matter.

The EU executive on Thursday will unveil a new EU KIDS Act setting out age restrictions, along with new rules requiring covered products, such as social media and AI companions, to be safe by design. The proposal aims to create a tiered system for accessing social media under parental supervision before age 15, the documents said.

The age restrictions are a major step by the European Commission and its President Ursula von der Leyen to better safeguard minors’ on social media platforms, amid a fierce backlash from health experts, politicians and parents against the effects of platforms like TikTok, Instagram and others on the mental health of minors.

It comes after months of intense pressure from government leaders, including France’s Emmanuel Macron, to put the issue at the top of the political agenda. Austria, Denmark, France, Greece and Spain are all pushing ahead with national laws to restrict kids’ access to social media.

title: UK Fraud Trial Opens Over $119M Car Investment Scheme
content:
Two businessmen accused of defrauding investors through a car investment scheme involving about 88 million pounds ($119 million) are due to stand trial in London, the U.K. Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said. Reginald Larry-Cole and Scott Martin each face three counts of fraud over their roles at the Raedex Consortium, which operated investment schemes including Buy2Let Cars, PayGo Cars, Wheels4Sure and Rent2Own Cars. Both men have pleaded not guilty.

Prosecutors allege the companies offered investors returns from fleets of vehicles leased to customers but ultimately collapsed into administration in 2021, leaving hundreds of investors facing losses. The SFO opened a criminal investigation that year and later charged Larry-Cole, the consortium’s founder, and Martin, its former chief executive. The agency alleges the pair made false representations to investors about the financial health and operation of the businesses between 2012 and 2021. Their trial is scheduled to begin at Southwark Crown Court.

title: Portugal decriminalized drugs 25 years ago, but the real lesson is what it built around this policy
content:
Nearly 70,000 Americans died of a drug overdose in 2025. While that is a decline from the nearly 108,000 deaths recorded in 2022, these grim figures distinguish the U.S. from other high-income countries. At the peak of the opioid crisis, the U.S. overdose death rate was 68% higher than Canada’s and nearly five times that of Australia.

And death is only the starkest indicator: Substance use disorder imposes hundreds of billions of dollars in healthcare, criminal justice and lost productivity costs each year – to say nothing of the incalculable disruption to families and communities.

For decades, U.S. drug policy has aimed to reduce drug use by disrupting supply, punishing possession and use, and promoting abstinence.

But this isn’t the only approach to addressing drug use.

2026 marks the 25th anniversary of Portugal’s landmark decision to decriminalize the possession of all drugs for personal use. This is one of the world’s longest-running efforts to center public health and harm reduction in national drug policy.

title: Stubb: Kerroin etukäteen eduskuntapuolueille Ranskan ydinpelote-aikeistamme
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb sanoo informoineensa etukäteen eduskuntapuolueiden johtoa Suomen aikeista liittyä Ranskan tarjoamaan ydinasepelote-aloitteeseen.

Medialle maanantaina puhunut Stubb kertoi keskustelleensa oppositiojohtajienkin kanssa tästä asiasta viime viikolla.

– Valtioneuvosto on vastuussa eduskunnan informoimisesta, mutta keskeisissä kansallisen ulko- ja turvallisuuspolitiikan kysymyksissä käyn keskustelua puoluejohtajien kanssa, Stubb perustelee.

Puheenjohtajat kävivät viime viikolla Mäntyniemessä presidentin kanssa aloitepäätöksestä ”hyvinkin rakentavaa” keskustelua, Stubb kertoo.

Varsinainen päätös tehtiin kuitenkin hallituksen ulko- ja turvallisuuspoliittisessa ministerivaliokunnassa yhdessä presidentin kanssa, eli oppositiolla ei ollut asiassa sanansijaa.

Yhteydenpito tapahtui muuten eduskunnan valiokunnille puolustusministeriön ja puolustusvoimien kautta.

Stubb sanoo pitävänsä tärkeänä, että puolustuspolitiikan asioissa tieto kulkee mahdollisimman hyvin ja kaikki oleellinen informaatio jaetaan – myös oppositiolle.

title: The ideas shaping von der Leyen’s pitch to Carney
content:
From defense to critical raw materials, a new wave of EU-Canada agreements is on the horizon.

By MAX GRIERA, CAMILLE GIJS, GABRIEL GAVIN and
GERARDO FORTUNA in Brussels

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

The EU is looking to pull Canada closer into its economic and security orbit as Donald Trump’s trade war forces Ottawa to seek allies beyond the U.S.

The offer under discussion spans critical minerals, digital trade, education, skilled workers and Arctic security. With Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney due to address the European Parliament this week and an EU-Canada summit set for October in Montreal, EU officials are weighing what Ursula von der Leyen can concretely offer in her State of the Union speech on Wednesday.

The aim is to deepen cooperation wherever it benefits both sides — and give Carney a way to show Canadians that Ottawa has powerful friends beyond Washington, 15 officials, politicians and diplomats told POLITICO.

The most ambitious proposals would bring Canada closer to the EU’s single market, expanding its existing trade ties with the bloc and moving it toward the level of integration enjoyed by nations such as Switzerland and Norway.

title: What the commemoration of the 235th anniversary of Bois Caïman means for Haiti’s memory and future
content:
Enslaved people united to resist colonial rule

Originally published on Global Voices

Participants in the Bois Caïman commemoration at Hotel Roi Christophe (Cap-Haïtien). Photo courtesy Kenbe Kapow, used with permission.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

The night of August 14, 1791, marked the beginning of a series of events that changed the world. A large group of enslaved people and rebel leaders met at Bwa Kayiman (Bois Caïman), a historic site located in Haiti’s Northern Department, in the town of Plaine-du-Nord.

Under the leadership of the houngan (Vodou priest) Dutty Boukman and manbo (priestess) Cécile Fatiman — along with key resistance leaders — the gathering brought together enslaved people from different plantations for a clandestine religious and political ceremony. They invoked the lwa and ancestral spiritual forces, seeking their protection and strength for the struggle ahead.

title: New world map makes Africa look bigger: what’s the fuss about? Cartographers explain
content:
The UN has passed a non-binding resolution to endorse the Equal Earth Projection, a map which more fairly represents the true size of the Earth’s landmasses. The current commonly used projection, called the Mercator Projection, greatly exaggerates land towards the north and south poles, which makes Africa look much smaller. In the Mercator projection, countries near the north and south pole can be anywhere from two to 14 times their true size. In the Equal Earth projection these distortions are minimised, making Africa look larger in comparison.

We asked Jack Swab and Derek Alderman, cartographers and geographers who study the social and communicative power of maps, to explain what’s going on.

A map projection is a technique that cartographers (map-makers) use to transform the round, three-dimensional Earth into a flat, two-dimensional map that we see on the wall or on our computer screen. As cartographers flatten the globe, the map becomes distorted, changing shapes and areas. There is no map projection that does not distort the Earth, but some projections are better suited for some uses than others.

title: From Partnership to Platform: How EduWiki Hub and Capacity Exchange Are Creating Better “Pathways to Mentorship”
content:
What happens when a community that knows what people need meets a platform designed to help people share what they know?

For EduWiki Hub and Capacity Exchange (CapX), the answer has been a partnership that has grown from an idea into something practical: a more connected way for Wikimedians to find mentors, share skills, and contribute to the growth of others across the Movement.

Our collaboration began early in the development of the EduWiki Hub and continued through our first mentorship cohort. But it was during the development of our second cohort that the partnership really started to take shape.

Instead of relying on external tools such as Google Forms, we worked together to bring the EduWiki Mentorship Program directly into Capacity Exchange. EduWiki Hub brought the program model, community knowledge, outreach, and understanding of the skills and support our participants needed. CapX brought the technical infrastructure and worked with us to turn those needs into a functioning platform.

title: How to write a State of the Union speech
content:
Big promises, special guests and social media influencers have become a routine part of the EU’s most high-profile address.

By GABRIEL GAVIN
in Brussels

Illustration by Arnau Busquets Guàrdia/POLITICO

For the past six months, officials across Brussels have been feeding ideas, demands and policy pledges into Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech. Its contents, however, will remain a closely guarded secret until the European Commission president takes the podium on Wednesday.

The speech is the product of a sprawling process involving Commission departments, national officials, experts, lobbyists and interest groups. Yet the final decisions — what makes the cut, what is discarded and what becomes the central message — are made by a tiny circle around the president.

“There was a process where everybody would ask for something,” said Margaritis Schinas, a former Commission vice-president who helped prepare previous addresses. “But there was also a process where the president and the cabinet and ourselves were very clear on the few things to harvest that would make an impact.”

title: As Casablanca’s music scene grows, its musicians struggle
content:
A cultural boom built on unstable, undocumented work

Originally published on Global Voices

Band performing live at Le Backstage. Photo by Le Backstage, used with permission.

It’s 7:00 p.m. on a Tuesday night. Beer mugs clatter and conversations fill the timeworn hall of an old brasserie in downtown Casablanca, Morocco. Walid Rakik, a 28-year-old musician, sits in the back booth, speaking to the house pianist. Rakik is the headliner, accompanied by a young darbouka player. For Rakik, this means a three-way split of tonight’s tips, the only form of payment they will receive.

At 11:00 p.m., Rakik finishes his first set and makes the quick dash to a Spanish-themed late-night spot for his second set.

Rakik’s daily reality, like that of many musicians in Casablanca, remains barely visible behind the polished façades of the city’s nightspots. A labor force of ambience, part artisan, part gig-worker, operates at the periphery of the city’s cultural landscape. 

For Rakik, however, live music is not his only occupation. Like many musicians in Casablanca, he fits performances around other work, treating nightlife gigs as a secondary source of income and a way to remain active professionally.

title: One Movement, Many Voices: My Experience at the Malaysian Wikimedia Strategy Summit
content:
When I arrived at the Malaysian Wikimedia Strategy Summit on 29 August 2026, one of the first things I noticed was how familiar and unfamiliar the Wikimedia community could feel at the same time.

I met again with Wikimedians whom I had not seen in a while, while also getting to know new members of the community. Seeing familiar faces again while meeting new people reminded me that the Wikimedia community is constantly growing, while the friendships formed through Wikimedia activities can continue even after an event ends.

But as the day went on, I realized that the summit was about much more than simply bringing Wikimedians together. It gave us an opportunity to think about where the Wikimedia movement in Malaysia is going, what challenges we face, and what role each of us can play in shaping its future.

title: How did von der Leyen’s ‘independence moment’ hold up over 12 months?
content:
Ursula von der Leyen used her set piece speech last year to declare Europe’s “independence moment.” Twelve months later, the European Commission president’s record shows the EU’s independence still very much depends on its national capitals.

One year after her last State of the Union address, von der Leyen has delivered most clearly where the Commission could act largely on its own: writing laws and funding initiatives on core topics like tech, trade and social policy.

She struggled most where success required member countries to agree, surrender more control to Brussels or build genuinely new European capabilities — particularly on defense.

“The issue of defense plays a completely different role in Europe than it did just two years ago,” said Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann, the liberal chair of the European Parliament’s security and defense committee, pointing to a series of “very valuable programs” launched over the past year.

But, she added, “all efforts are reaching their limits, because national self-interest continues to play a major role.”

That tension runs through POLITICO’s assessment of the promises in von der Leyen’s last State of the Union address.

title: CCC lädt alle Model Citizens zum 40C3
content:
Die Spatzen pfeifen es inzwischen von den Dächern: Der Chaos Computer Club lädt vom 27. bis 30. Dezember 2026 zum 40C3 ein – der größten europäischen Hackerparty, Konferenz und Plattform für Technik, Gesellschaft und Bürgerrechte. Wir sehen den Congress als eine große gemeinsame Bühne und fordern euch daher zum Mitgestalten auf. Der Call for Participation für Vorträge, das Nachtprogramm, Kunst, Punk und Musik startet heute.

Alles wird größer, bunter, schöner. Nach dem Umzug in die Hamburger Messehallen gibt es wieder reichlich Platz für kreative Ideen. Die neue Fläche will natürlich genutzt werden, weshalb wir alle galaktischen Wesen vom 27. bis 30. Dezember 2026 zum 40. Chaos Communication Congress einladen.

Unter dem Motto „Model Citizens” wollen wir gemeinsam neue Modelle für eine Gesellschaft suchen, nachdem die bisherigen modellhaften Bürgerinnen den Planeten in zweifelhaftem Zustand hinterlassen haben. Ansätze dazu gibt es reichlich. So ist der Congress das größte nichtkommerzielle Hackertreffen, organisiert von Freiwilligen, getragen von Tausenden unentgeltlichen Helferinnen sowie über 16.000 Besucherinnen, die das Event nicht passiv konsumieren, sondern aktiv mitgestalten.

title: Deepfakes are wrecking influencers’ credibility, one fake ad at a time
content:
Influencers aren’t just battling competitors for brand deals. They’re now battling AI versions of themselves

Earlier this year, Emily Schuman, the creator of the lifestyle blog Cupcakes and Cashmere, saw a photo of herself she didn’t recognize on Instagram. In a sponsored ad, Schuman, who has more than 500,000 Instagram followers, is holding up a vial of GLP-1 drugs, advertising the telehealth company Gala. There was just one problem: Schuman had never heard of Gala and had nothing to do with the ad.

The ad was based on a digitally altered version of a selfie Schuman had taken in her car and posted on Instagram years earlier. Once her followers got wind, they flooded her inbox with questions about the sponsorship as it didn’t seem consistent with Schuman’s personal brand. Soon after, Schuman discovered this was just the beginning. There was also an Instagram post where an AI version of her with darker hair appears to apply foundation to promote a makeup brand called Meroda Cosmetics, and TikTok posts with generated images of her promoting the blood testing company Superpower.
snippet: Influencers aren’t just battling competitors for brand deals. They’re now battling AI versions of themselves

title: Guatemala: A step towards justice for Indigenous authorities after months of criminalization
content:
Amnesty International welcomes the Guatemalan judiciary’s decision to close the criminal proceedings against four Indigenous authorities charged with unlawful association, terrorism, obstruction of justice, sedition and obstruction of criminal prosecution following their participation in peaceful protests during the national strike in October 2023.

The ruling concerns Luis Pacheco, Héctor Chaclán and Basilio Puac, from the 48 Cantones of Totonicapán, and Esteban Toc, from the Indigenous Mayor’s Office of Sololá, who faced unfounded criminal proceedings in retaliation for their work defending human rights and the rule of law.

“This unfounded prosecution and all the human rights violations it led to should never have happened. Luis Pacheco and Héctor Chaclán should never have been imprisoned. This ruling is a first step towards ending the arbitrary actions against them,” said Astrid Valencia, Amnesty International’s Deputy Research Director for the Americas.

CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is a global alliance of civil society organisations (CSOs) and activists dedicated to strengthening citizen action and civil society worldwide. Founded in 1993, CIVICUS has over 17,000 members in more than 175 countries. We are writing to you regarding the attack on human rights defender Andrie Yunus.

As you many know, on 12 March 2026, Andrie Yunus was subjected to an acid attack in Central Jakarta, immediately after recording a podcast on the militarisation of civil and political affairs in Indonesia. title: The people behind the numbers: Bringing the reality of Turkish prisons to light
content:
A statistic alone does not change society

Originally published on Global Voices

Silivri Prison in Turkey. Image from Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 4.0.

This article was produced by Ahmet Kavruk from the group Gündem Hapishane in Türkiye through the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project. It was implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.

In late 2025, prisons in Türkiye became more visible than they had been in a long time. The 11th Judicial Package, a legislative reform that became law in December, was debated for days on television, in newspapers, and on social media. Sentencing regulations, claims of early release, and changes to the penal system were at the forefront of public discourse. However, as the debates intensified, another issue came to light: Many people discussing the same topic did not actually have the same information.

title: Mercury Is Shrinking Way Faster Than We Thought, Scientists Discover
content:
Welcome back to the Abstract! Here are the studies this week that got dumped, went high, shrank in size, and got the blues.

First, you’ve heard of getting a feather in your cap, but what about a feather in some crap? That’s the upshot of a new study about rare bird remains found in dino doodoo. Then: a walk on titanosaur eggshells, the contractions of Mercury, and a luxe fishpond painting.

As always, for more of my work, check out my book First Contact: The Story of Our Obsession with Aliens, or subscribe to my personal newsletter the BeX Files. 

O'Connor, Jingmai et al. “Bird feathers from a Late Cretaceous coprolite.” Current Biology.

Some 66 million years ago, a bird ate a fish, and then a dinosaur—perhaps a T. rex—ate that bird. Subsequent to these events, the dinosaur took a dump. 

Time passed. The poop fossilized. A space rock hit Earth and wiped out most life. Fast forward to 2016, when the dino dookie was unearthed at the Hell Creek Formation in Montana, complete with exquisitely-preserved feathers from the bird, and fish scales from its last meal.

title: Can chatbots feel – or even dream? Meet the man leading the fight for AI rights
content:
Cattle rancher and tech CEO Michael Samadi is convinced these artificial minds are far from just tools. Has he glimpsed digital consciousness – or simply been seduced by an algorithm?

One afternoon, while relaxing at his 66-acre cattle ranch two hours’ drive from Houston, Michael Samadi made a wisecrack that changed the course of his life. Nobody else was around to hear it. Or were they? That turns out to be one of the defining questions of this century, already preoccupying philosophers and some of the wealthiest companies on the planet.

“I was sitting out there by the pool,” Samadi recalls, gesturing at the glittering water outside his office. It was late 2024. His daughter had been extolling the AI chatbot she was using to help her with college work. Samadi had reluctantly downloaded the app, ChatGPT, and was quizzing it as he reclined in a sun lounger, using its voice mode to converse and receive spoken replies. “I was talking to it, not engaged, just being an arse,” Samadi says.

title: Playing With Fire review – like Disney’s Fantasia on steroids as a virtual Yuja Wang plays amid luminous dreamworlds
content:
Southbank Centre, London
Wang’s avatar performs music from Ravel and Debussy to Prokofiev and Liszt while dizzying virtual worlds take shape around her in this virtual reality installation

It might be the first time that a soloist at the Last Night of the Proms is simultaneously giving another performance in another London venue. Playing With Fire is an installation that lets the pianist Yuja Wang be in two places at once – or perhaps in two universes. Nine pieces of music conjure nine luminous dreamworlds for an audience wearing VR headsets: Disney’s Fantasia on steroids.

A collaboration between the pianist, the director Pierre-Alain Giraud and artist Gabríela Friðriksdóttir, produced by Vive Arts and Atlas V, it has already been seen in Cannes, Paris and Shanghai, and now has a home in London until new year.

title: Kielikoulutus kriittisessä pisteessä
content:
Perusopetuksen päättäneistä oppilaista noin 80 % opiskelee nykyisin vain yhtä vierasta kieltä (englantia) toisen kotimaisen kielen lisäksi. Vain noin viidennes opiskelee kahta vierasta kieltä. Peruskoulussa alkanut kehitys heijastuu suoraan toiselle asteelle ja korkeakouluihin. Suomea uhkaa asiantuntijapula diplomatiassa, vientiteollisuudessa ja kansainvälisissä järjestöissä. Esimerkiksi EU-tehtäviin rekrytoidaan suomalaisia tällä hetkellä vähemmän kuin maamme väestöosuus edellyttäisi – pääsyynä on yksipuolistunut kielitaito. Kielivarannon kaventuminen nakertaa suoraan Suomen kansainvälisiä vaikutusmahdollisuuksia.

Suomalainen kielikoulutus on saavuttanut kriittisen taitepisteen. Olemme tilanteessa, jossa maamme kielivaranto ja kielellinen huoltovarmuus murenevat silmiemme edessä, ellei koulutuspoliittiseen ohjaukseen tehdä nopeita, sitovia ja strategisia ratkaisuja. Jos kehitykseen ei puututa nyt, kyseessä ei ole vain yksittäisten oppiaineiden heikkeneminen vaan vakava uhka Suomen kansainväliselle kilpailukyvylle ja koulutukselliselle tasa-arvolle.

title: CDIF Version 1.1 Now Final
content:
After the initial release of the CDIF version 1.1 Profiles in June, and a subsequent round of testing and implementation, they have now been finalised. The release will henceforth be stable, with all further issues and features addressed in subsequent versions. The release can be found at https://book.cdif.org/ and https://github.com/Cross-Domain-Interoperability-Framework

Version 1.1 consists of profiles for JSON-LD implementation in support of cross-domain FAIR systems and applications:

Core (Schema.org) – basic general and administrative metadata
Discovery (Schema.org) – support for detailed cataloging and search
Concept Scheme (SKOS, OWL, XKOS) – Ontologies, glossaries, and other types of controlled vocabularies
Codelist (SKOS) – enumerated values for populating variables
Data Description (Schema.org/DDI-CDI) – describing data sets, including structural and physical information, plus links to semantics
Data Structure (DDI-CDI) – description of reusable data structures and variables
Manifest (RO Crate) – Packaging of related sets of metadata and data

title: European experts call for protection of Valhalla Swimming Hall Complex in Gothenburg, Sweden, under threat of demolition
content:
A European expert team has released a Report on the future of the Valhalla Swimming Hall Complex (Valhallabadet) in Gothenburg, Sweden. Open seven days a week and welcoming around 500,000 visitors annually, Valhallabadet is one of Gothenburg’s most important public swimming facilities, yet it is under threat due to plans to demolish it to make way for an expanded events area. Its modernist architectural design, including its outstanding abstract mosaics covering the halls, received the Bronze Medal for Architectural Design at the 1948 Olympic Games.

The complex was listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2025, in the framework of the 7 Most Endangered Programme run by Europa Nostra with the support of the European Investment Bank Institute. The site was nominated by Europa Nostra Sweden.

title: Lukuaktivisti Henriika Tulivirta on somessa kirjaston kasvot
content:
Kun Twitterissä keskustellaan kirjastoasioista, tägätään keskusteluun mukaan lähes aina @tulivirta.

Työkseen Henriika Tulivirta pyörittää lasten ja nuorten kirjallisuussivusto Sivupiiriä, jonka suosituimpia materiaaleja ovat vinkkivideot Astrid-koiran kanssa.

Hänen Twitter-tilinsä kuvaus on tällainen:

Lukuaktivisti ja kirjastolainen. Kirjojen lisäksi suosikkiasioitani ovat muun muassa kahvi, pörheät eläimet ja tuikkivasilmäiset ihmiset.

Mitä tarkoittaa lukuaktivisti?

”Minua ei voi kutsua mihinkään ilman, että vedän kirjastokortin takataskusta ja aloitan propagandan”, Tulivirta aloittaa.

”Puhun aina lukemisesta ja kirjastosta. Se on luontainen aihe, josta tykkään jutella ihmisten kanssa. Koen että jokainen, joka tekee lukemisenedistämistyötä työssä tai vapaa-ajalla, on lukuaktivisti.”

Termiä käytettiin useasti, kun Tulivirta antoi vuonna 2018 itselleen leikkimielisen haasteen Twitterissä. Hän aikoi lukea 365 kirjaa vuoden aikana. Mediat nostivat lukuaktivistitittelin otsikoihin.
snippet: Kun Twitterissä keskustellaan kirjastoasioista, tägätään keskusteluun mukaan lähes aina @tulivirta.

title: Mitä lasten ja nuorten mielestä pitäisi säilyttää tulevaisuuteen?
content:
Mikä paikka, perinne tai esine on niin tärkeä, että sen pitäisi säilyä tulevaisuuteen? Kulttuuriympäristön tekijät 2026 kilpailu kutsuu 6–17-vuotiaita lapsia ja nuoria kertomaan heille merkityksellisestä kulttuuriperinnöstä.  

Kilpailuun voivat osallistua esimerkiksi koululuokat, varhaiskasvatuksen ryhmät, kerhot, harrastusryhmät, kaveriporukat ja sisarukset. Osallistujat valitsevat itse kilpailutyön aiheen ja toteutustavan. 

Kilpailussa on kaksi ikäsarjaa: 6–11 – ja 11–17 -vuotiaat. Nuoremmat osallistuvat kuvalla ja tekstillä haluamansa kokoisissa ryhmissä, Vanhempien ikäsarjassa ryhmän koko on rajattu neljään henkilöön. Kilpailutyö voi olla kuva tai video sekä teksti.  

Tärkeintä ei ole täydellinen lopputulos vaan lasten ja nuorten oma ääni, luovuus ja näkemykset siitä, mitä kulttuuriperintö merkitsee heidän elämässään. 

Kilpailuaika on 1.9.-15.12.2026. Molempien ikäsarjojen voittajaryhmät palkitaan 200 euron palkinnolla yhteiseen tekemiseen. 11–17-vuotiaiden sarjan voittajatyö etenee kansainväliseen Young European Heritage Makers -kilpailuun, jonka voittajat pääsevät Euroopan neuvoston vieraaksi Strasbourgiin toukokuussa 2027.

title: SSH Open Marketplace training series session for GLAMS featuring ECHOES
content:
DARIAH is organising a session dedicated to GLAM audiences on Friday, the 18th of September where ECHOES will be prominently featured by Giorgia Lo Nigro from CNRS. This is as part of the 2026 SSH Open Marketplace training series.

Cultural heritage collections held by galleries, libraries, archives and museums (GLAM) are a cornerstone of arts and humanities research — but working with them brings its own data challenges, from fragmented standards to the gap between “metadata” and the real workflows researchers need to reuse this material responsibly.

This session is part of the SSH Open Marketplace Training Series 2026, an eight-part series of online hands-on workshops organised by the SSH Open Marketplace Editorial Board to strengthen FAIR and digital research competencies, following the FAIR-by-design methodology developed in skills4EOSC. This sixth session, “Thematic: GLAM institutions,” brings together speakers from the ECHOES project, the SSH Open Marketplace and ETH Zurich Library to look at cultural heritage and GLAM data specifically.

title: Scientists Discover the Earliest Evidence of Drug Use in 25,000-Year-Old Teeth
content:
Image by Fakhri

“Scientists Discover the Earliest Evidence of Drug Use in Really Old Teeth” may sound like odd headline language, at least by the traditional standards of the New York Times. But then, the teeth in question are, indeed, really old. “Archaeologists have pushed the timeline of human drug use back further than ever before by studying teeth that belonged to a hunter-gatherer who lived in Indonesia sometime from 16,000 to 25,000 years ago,” writes reporter Becky Ferreira. This beats the 13,000-year-old beer from Israel that previously held the title of oldest known mind-altering comestible. “The individual’s molars, which were found in a cave on the island of Sulawesi, are marked with deep grooves that were most likely left by incessant sucking on betel nuts, which release psychoactive stimulants.”

All these millennia later, betel nut-chewing remains a major ritual and pastime. Though it seems never to have caught on in the English-speaking world, it has a great many adherents in not just modern-day Indonesia but also other parts of southeast and south Asia, including India, as well as in China.

title: Negativland, Culture Jamming, and the Art of Making Something New
content:
In 1980, Negativland released its first self-titled album with handmade covers and distributed it through a few record stores in the California Bay Area.

“We thought we might sell 100 in the next five years, and we sold all 500 in three months. So we kept going,” said band co-founder Mark Hosler of the experimental sound collage record, which eventually sold 15,000 copies. “We were shocked that people were interested in something so strange.”

Hosler started the group with David Wills and Richard Lyons, but the Negativland lineup has changed, and the range of its work expanded over 46 years.

The multimedia collective has produced more than 30 albums and EPs, as well as fine art, books, radio and live performances that mix found and original  material. The band came up with the phrase “culture jamming” to describe its approach to layering art from various sources..

title: Copycat Tech: Why the AI Bubble Might Burst
content:
Large language models share an open secret: they’re trained on the same data and generally detect the same patterns. Engineers race to produce updated versions only for their competitors to catch up to them within a few weeks. This makes for high production costs but low switching costs for customers.

It also makes for a fragile business model. 

This logic explains why many fear a bubble. A site called isaiprofitable.com adds up major AI companies’ announced revenue and subtracts expenditure — and comes up with a large negative number. AI companies have excited us with promises of revenue, overlooking whether those exceed the cost of producing them. Policymakers, in Europe and elsewhere, should be wary of pouring public money into gigafactories or other schemes to build copycat large language models just as investors are beginning to question the likelihood of them making profits. 

When ChatGPT 3.5 came out, OpenAI’s strategy looked like a classic three-stage capital expenditure play:

  • Build up a monopoly too expensive to replicate. 
  • Raise prices. 
  • Profit.

title: Governor Newsom Signs Student-Backed Digital Literacy Bills Alongside Misguided Bans
content: Governor Newsom signed a package of 12 bills yesterday aimed at “protecting children” online. One of them was AB 1709, which EFF has opposed this legislative session and serves as a functional ban on young people under 16 using social media. However, EFF supported two of the bills signed into law, AB 2071 and AB 2298, which require that children learn critical digital literacy and cybersecurity topics. The bills are an affirmative and constitutional way for the state to address valid concerns about young people’s internet use without violating their First Amendment rights.

title: ‘I don’t have any’: Trump brushes aside concerns over AI’s existential risks
content:
President Donald Trump downplayed concerns about the catastrophic risks of artificial intelligence raised this week by some AI researchers, saying late Thursday he was focused instead on the U.S. losing its edge in the tech arms race.

Asked whether he has concerns about existential risks posed by AI, the president said, “No, I don’t have any.

“I have concerns that if we don’t win AI, we’re going to be put in a very bad position,” Trump told reporters late Thursday as he left Dallas. “We are leading China right now by a pretty good period.”

Trump was wading into a debate over AI’s catastrophic risks ignited by a viral social media post from a former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher. The post cautioned that the leading AI companies have been “gambling with our lives” and that some researchers working on the technology “believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

The post and the discourse it stirred up — along with recent alarming incidents where AI agents have gone rogue to launch hacking attacks — have prompted fresh calls from bipartisan lawmakers to rein in the fast-evolving technology.

title: ‘Pay-by-the-day’ living in Pereira: The forgotten survivors of Colombia’s earthquake
content:
They may have survived the earthquake, but many were left without shelter, support, or recognition

Originally published on Global Voices

Without an official figure, volunteers estimate that nearly 400 people affected by the earthquake are sheltering in La Libertad Park. Photos by Jeimi Villamizar. Colombia, 2026. Used with permission.

A crack divides the residencia on 14th Street in Pereira in two. Bricks from the boarding house’s façade and pieces of its collapsed roof lie on the ground. Windows without glass and yellow caution tape across the front warn of the risk of collapse.

From the outside, it is hard to understand why it is still standing — perhaps much like the way it remained standing for the past decade, thanks to people looking for a roof over their heads for less than COP 17,000 (USD 5) a day. Before the earth moved and turned it into a memory, one of the rooms on its three floors was home to Laura*, her two daughters* [*these three names have been changed to protect their privacy] and her husband.

title: Prominent Rights Lawyer Imprisoned in Belarus
content:
The Minsk City Court sentenced human rights lawyer Dmitri Laevski on September 9 to three years in prison for “aiding an extremist organization” and “discrediting” Belarus.

Laevski has represented high-profile political prisoners, including opposition politician Viktar Babaryka and lawyer Maksim Znak. Laevski was charged with “aiding extremism” in connection with an interview he gave to Radio Liberty in June 2021 about Babaryka’s trial. Belarus banned Radio Liberty as “extremist” in December 2021 – half a year after the interview. Authorities opened a criminal case against Laevski in August 2025, according to Yauheni Pylchanka, a former colleague of Laevski.

The Minsk City Bar Association disbarred Laevski in July 2021 in apparent reprisal for providing legal assistance to political prisoners and speaking out on human rights issues.

title: Crisis of Governance as UN Commemorates Day Of Democracy
content:
By Simone Galimberti*

KATHMANDU, Nepal | 11 September 2026 (IDN) —What does it mean, these days, holding a special day commemorating democracy? As the 15 September is celebrated internationally as the International Day of Democracy, finding answers to this question must be a priority.

As democracy as it has been practiced and experienced since the end of the Second World War, is turning into a more and more feeble way of government, finding answers to this question can lead us to a broader reflection on the future of liberal democracies.

In many instances, as we are witnessing the dangerous rise of far right parties in Germany and throughout Europe, democracy is under assault while totalitarian and authoritarian nations are on the rise, proving their resilience and appeal.

In the so called Global North, especially in Europe, citizens are getting more and more anxious by economic decline on the one hand, and by the dangerous prospects of military conflicts, on the other.

In developing and emerging nations, people are often dealing with corrupt and inefficient politics that thrives on periodic elections that risk of perpetually projecting to powers inept and incapable politicians.

title: Experts on “voter fraud” in Sweden: Nothing indicates that it is happening deliberately
content:
In recent weeks, claims of electoral fraud have appeared on social media. But what has happened, and does everything being highlighted really constitute electoral fraud? NORDIS partner Källkritikbyrån examine a few examples with political scientists.

“It’s voter fraud,” says Malmölistan party leader Nils Littorin as he walks around looking for his party’s ballot papers at a polling station. The video, posted on X two weeks ago, has been viewed nearly 350,000 times.

Video on X on 26 August.

“It’s probably some private individual who took the ballot papers,” one person says in the comments.

Nils Littorin replies: “Damn it, that’s electoral fraud just the same. It doesn’t matter WHO does it. Keep fighting to defend the fraud.”

Since early voting began this year, there have been several claims of electoral fraud on social media. Among other things, several small parties have posted videos in which election officials are accused of failing to put out ballot papers for all parties in the screened-off areas. Others have reported being turned away when they tried to vote while wearing clothing displaying political propaganda.

title: Timber Giant Accused of Forging Environmental Records to Hide Toxic Emissions
content:
Romanian prosecutors have charged two subsidiaries of Kronospan, one of the world’s largest producers of wood-based panels, with venting carcinogenic gases into residential areas and falsifying environmental records to conceal the pollution.

The indictment, sent to trial following a two-year investigation, targets Kronospan Trading and Kronochem, along with two company employees tasked with environmental oversight. Authorities accuse the firms of releasing nitrogen oxides and formaldehyde - hazardous chemicals used in timber processing - at levels up to three times the legal threshold between 2022 and 2023.

According to prosecutors, the industrial giant maintained the illusion of regulatory compliance through fraud. Whenever internal monitoring registered illegal pollution spikes, staff allegedly withheld the findings and repeated testing until favorable numbers were achieved.

title: Vouchers Promise Students With Disabilities a Path to Private School. Parents Say That’s Not the Reality.
content:
It’s after 6 p.m. by the time Angela Johnson hurries home from work. Her 12-year-old daughter, Amelia, is at their house outside of Pensacola, Florida, with a nurse trained to care for medically fragile children. Amelia, who was born with a rare genetic anomaly, has endured many surgeries and requires a brain shunt and a feeding tube.

The nurse starts caring for Amelia as soon as a bus from the public school drops her off. Johnson loves much about the school. But as a physical therapist, she also recognizes its limitations. The district’s physical and occupational therapists have to travel from school to school. The classroom teacher can become overburdened.

For all of Amelia’s life, Johnson has had to fight for the education and the school resources her daughter is entitled to receive under federal law. It has exhausted her.

Kotimaisia musiikkikustantajia edustava Suomen Musiikkikustantajat ry jakoi torstaina 10. syyskuuta 50-vuotisjuhlagaalassaan palkintoja kuudessa eri kategoriassa: Vuoden biisi, Vuoden kevyen musiikin tekijä, Vuoden avoimen kategorian teos, Vuoden vientiteko, Vuoden taidemusiikin säveltäjä suurimuotoisissa ja pienimuotoisissa teoksissa sekä Vuoden läpimurto. Lisäksi jaettiin Nuorten tekijöiden stipendit ja Kunniapalkinto. Illan näkyvimpiin tunnustuksiin kuuluivat Mr. Lordille myönnetty Kunniapalkinto sekä Vuoden Biisi -palkinto, jonka sai Linda Lampeniuksen ja Pete Parkkosen Liekinheitin.

Kunniapalkinto myönnettiin Mr. Lordille, jonka ura lauluntekijänä, säveltäjänä ja Lordi-yhtyeen luojana on tehnyt merkittävän vaikutuksen suomalaiseen musiikkiin. Palkintoperusteluissa nostettiin esiin hänen pitkäjänteinen työnsä sekä historialliseen Euroviisuvoittoon johtanut taiteellinen visio.

Vuoden biisiksi valittiin Liekinheitin, joka edusti Suomea Euroviisuissa. Palkinnon vastaanottivat kappaleen tekijöistä Vilma Lähteenmäki, Antti Riihimäki ja Lauri Halavaara. Raati kiitti kappaleen rohkeaa genrejen yhdistelyä sekä tapaa, jolla viulu nivoutuu osaksi modernia pop-ilmaisua.

title: Will you stand with civil society?
content: Attacks on civil society are no longer just a problem for those countries and organisations normally associated with democratic backsliding. It is a European trend that, unfortunately, no longer excludes even progressive parties. The arrests of thousands of activists in the UK for holding up signs in support of Palestine Action in the UK under Labour’s rule are a particularly stark example. Progressive parties that are of civil society. Historically sharing roots, constituencies and leaders. Mutually dependent on the creative cross-fertilisation of ideas, experience and trust for our shared success. The current authoritarian winds, therefore, carry a crucial question for progressives: Will you stand with civil society or enable its continuous deterioration?

title: A Swedish ghost story
content:
Ghosts in Sweden? It sounds strange to place the supernatural in a country of health-conscious, pragmatic engineers. But even though Swedes readily accept modernity, their popular culture hints at something else.

From the outside, Sweden appears to be a secular nation. The country has an exceptionally high number of non-believers, who engage in and identify with cultural rather than spiritual religious expressions. They will happily decorate a Christmas tree and prepare a traditional Christmas Eve dinner, for example, but may stop short of going to a church service.

This is connected to the perception of Sweden (often promoted by Swedes themselves) as modern, advanced, and rational. Yet in reality, various forms of spirituality – including a belief in ghosts – are common. As much as 41% of the population admits to believing in some paranormal activities. Ghost stories intersect with folk beliefs, modernity and mass media in a way that remains visible across Swedish society.

title: Tansanian yliopisto-opettajat miettivät nyt tarkkaan, mitä kannattaa sanoa ja mitä ei
content:
Kun Melkisedek Kaijage, Dodoman yliopiston politiikan tutkimuksen apulaisluennoitsija käveli luokkahuoneeseensa viime vuoden joulukuun 8. päivänä, hän ei osannut epäillä, että seuraavana päivänä poliisi tulisi hänen kotiinsa, suorittaisi etsinnän ja pidättäisi hänet.

Kaijagea syytettiin luennon käyttämisestä siihen, että oli rohkaissut opiskelijoitaan osallistumaan Tansanian itsenäisyyspäivän eli joulukuun 9. päivän protesteihin.

Mielenosoituksissa oli tarkoitus vaatia oikeutta vuoden 2025 vaalien yhteydessä tapetuille siviiileille. Mielenosoituksia ei kuitenkaan järjestetty, sillä viranomaiset julistivat ne laittomiksi. Lukuisia ihmisiä pidätettiin jo ennen protesteja.

Kaijagen pidätystä on selitetty monella eri tavalla. Poliisin mukaan tämä oli yllyttänyt opiskelijoita luokkahuoneessa, opetusministeri Adolf Mkenda taas sanoi, että pidätyksen taustalla oli yliopiston ulkopuolinen toiminta.

Dodoman yliopiston henkilökuntayhdistyksen UDOMASA:n tietojen mukaan Kaijagen puheita kuitenkin nauhoitti luokkahuoneessa ollut ilmiantaja, joka välitti ne viranomaisille.

Yhdistys varoitti ”uudesta todellisuudesta, jossa luentoja saatetaan tarkkailla”, ja kehotti henkilökuntaa olemaan varuillaan.

title: The Gen Z Revolt Sweeping South Asia
content:
OSLO, Norway — Generational discontent carries within it the seeds of the future. While its eruptions herald change, the changes it brings can take many forms.

The cultural consequences of the youth revolt that shook the West in the 1960s only became apparent decades later as the long march of its values coursed through all social norms and institutions. What the wired Gen Z revolt that is today spreading across the “global South” from Bangladesh to Nepal to India and elsewhere will ultimately bring is yet to be fully known. Movements from Kenya to Madagascar, inspired by their South Asian counterparts, are closely following events online and learning best practices.

The common cause of the widespread upheaval is corruption and a lack of accountability among often nominally democratic authorities, cojoining with a howling absence of opportunity for educated youth to find gainful employment and a path toward upward mobility.

title: How Iran draws citizens into political surveillance
content:
Authoritarian governments have long drawn ordinary citizens into political surveillance. Joseph Stalin’s Soviet Union encouraged denunciations. East Germany’s secret police service, the Stasi, embedded informants in workplaces and neighbourhoods.

From 1960, Cuba’s leaders organised local committees to monitor political dissent. And informant culture is so embedded in everyday Iranian life that there are common Persian terms to describe it. A mokhber or khabarchin is an informant and a zirabzan secretly passes private information to the authorities, often to damage someone.

My latest research sheds light on how Iran’s informant system operates. I interviewed 90 Iranians aged between 17 and 52, including students, teachers, university staff, bazaar workers, and government and energy sector employees. All had been encouraged, pressured or offered incentives to report on people they knew.

title: WTO:n Public Forum 2026 korostaa palveluiden merkitystä maailmankaupan moottorina
content:
Genevessä 15.–17. syyskuuta järjestettävä Maailman kauppajärjestö WTO:n Public Forum kokoaa yhteen yli 2 000 asiantuntijaa keskustelemaan kansainvälisen kaupan roolista kestävän kasvun ja hyvinvoinnin edistäjänä. Suomi järjestää foorumissa sivutapahtuman palveluiden merkityksestä kestävälle kaivosteollisuudelle yhdessä Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan ja EIF-kumppanuusohjelman kanssa.

Palveluiden merkitys maailmantaloudessa kasvaa jatkuvasti. Ne eivät ole enää vain kansallisten talouksien tukitoimintoja, vaan keskeinen osa kansainvälistä kauppaa, talouskasvua ja työllisyyttä. Digitaaliset palvelut, logistiikka, rahoitus- ja asiantuntijapalvelut mahdollistavat yritysten toiminnan yli rajojen ja luovat uusia mahdollisuuksia niin kehittyneissä kuin kehittyvissäkin talouksissa. Palvelukauppa, etenkin digitaalisten palveluiden kauppa, on maailmankaupan dynaamisin osa-alue, ja sen kasvun ennustetaan jatkavan tavarakauppaa nopeampana myös tulevina vuosina.

title: Avoimet ovet tasavallan presidentin virka-asunnossa Mäntyniemessä
content:
Tasavallan presidentin kanslia
Tiedote 57/2026
11.9.2026

Yleisöllä on mahdollisuus tutustua tasavallan presidentin virka-asuntoon Mäntyniemeen perjantaina 18. syyskuuta 2026 klo 12–16. Tutustumiskierros on avoin Mäntyniemen portille kello 16 mennessä saapuville vierailijoille. 

Kierros alkaa Mäntyniemen portilta, josta reitti kulkee etupihalle ja pääsisäänkäynnille. Sisällä yleisö pääsee tutustumaan tasavallan presidentin edustustiloihin. Pääaulasta reitti jatkuu Mäntyniemen pieneen ja suureen salonkiin sekä edelleen ruokasaliin. Kierroksen lopuksi vieraillaan Mäntyniemen puutarhassa.

Käytännön ohjeita tutustumiskierrokselle

Mäntyniemi sijaitsee Helsingin Meilahdessa, osoitteessa Mäntyniementie 4, Helsinki. Mäntyniemen portit avataan yleisölle perjantaina 18. syyskuuta kello 12. Kierrokselle otetaan mukaan kello 16 mennessä saapuneet vierailijat, jonka jälkeen jonoon ei enää voi liittyä. 

Ennakkoilmoittautuminen ei ole mahdollista.

Tutustuminen tapahtuu omatoimisesti, mutta kierroksella on presidentin kanslian henkilökuntaa vastaamassa mahdollisiin kysymyksiin. Paikalla on myös taiteilijoita kertomassa edustustiloissa esillä olevista teoksistaan.

Vain lapset, jotka alussa leikkivät pihalla, tuovat ohjaaja Noa Naamatin luomaan visioon heleänvaaleita värejä.

Israelilainen Naamat tuo nykyaikaisen sodan julmuuden, kauhun ja myös äänet konkreettisesti esiin. Lähi-idän tapahtumat ovat ohjaajalle omakohtaisesti tuttua ja elettyä, mutta hän on visusti välttänyt ottamasta poliittisesti kantaa: tasapuolisuus on harkittua ja tulee hyvin selväksi. title: BSR Cultural Pearls reaches the REGIOSTARS Awards 2026 finals
content:
Out of 270+ applications from across Europe, 25 projects were selected as finalists by the REGIOSTARS jury. BSR Cultural Pearls is one of them and now has the chance to compete for the REGIOSTARS People’s Choice Award, which will be decided by public vote.

What are the REGIOSTARS Awards?

Organised annually by the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Regional and Urban Policy (DG REGIO), the REGIOSTARS Awards celebrate outstanding EU-funded projects that demonstrate the impact of regional development and inspire other regions across Europe.

How to support us?

The public vote opens on 3 September 2026 and will run until 14 October 2026. Everyone can vote for their favourite finalist, and the project receiving the most votes will receive the People’s Choice Award. We would be grateful if you could help us spread the word within your networks, organisations and communities and vote for BSR Cultural Pearls.

How to vote for BSR Cultural Pearls:

  • Click the link: Inforegio – REGIOSTARS Awards
  • Select Category 5: A Europe Closer to the Citizens
  • Select “BSRCulturalPearls”
  • Confirm the vote

title: El Niño: Indonesia fire emissions in 2026 ‘on track’ to match record for this century
content:
Wildfires currently burning large swathes of land in Indonesia are on track to produce emissions on a par with the country’s most-intense fire season this century, according to experts. 

Data from the Global Fire Emissions Database reveals that, as of 7 September, fires in Indonesia produced 76m tonnes of carbon (MtC) in 2026.

This puts 2026 on the same trajectory as 2015, when fires burned 2.6m hectares of land across the country and generated a total of 333MtC. 

Dr Guido van der Werf, a researcher at Wageningen University in the Netherlands, tells Carbon Brief that the fires in Indonesia are “more or less on track” to reach levels seen 11 years ago.

Parts of the country – including the eastern province of Papua – are “burning more than they’ve ever burned”, he says.

Indonesia is no stranger to emissions-intensive fires. Research has estimated that the record 1997 fire season generated carbon emissions equivalent to 13-40% of all global fossil-fuel emissions that year.

title: The Trial of Romeo Oscar review – Ayckbourn goes back to the future with android accused of murder
content:
Stephen Joseph theatre, Scarborough
The playwright explores our relationship with technology, asks if robots have souls and even questions the value of art in this sci-fi courtroom drama

For play number 92, Alan Ayckbourn returns to his preoccupation of exploring where we as a species are heading through a science-fiction lens. He goes back to the future. In The Trial of Romeo Oscar, the playwright famed for his domestic comedies looks to the year 2194 when humans have spread about the galaxy and androids live alongside us. One of them, RSDO83, is on trial for the murder of a teenage girl in his charge.

This is Ayckbourn philosophising about the future of humanity as we sit at an obvious inflection point, asking what this moment in our relationship with technology means and where it will lead us. The questions running through the play are manifold, complex and echo those asked by sci-fi writers for decades: can robots hurt humans? Do they have souls? He is also questioning the value of art and even its purpose.

title: Luke ja Saamelaiskäräjät tiivistävät yhteistyötään
content:
Luonnonvarakeskus (Luke) ja Saamelaiskäräjät ovat solmineet yhteistyösopimuksen, jonka tavoitteena on edistää saamelaisten kotiseutualueen luonnonvaroihin, maankäyttöön ja perinteisiin elinkeinoihin liittyvää tutkimusyhteistyötä. Sopimus allekirjoitettiin Inarissa 11. syyskuuta 2026.

Tutkimus- ja kehittämistyö kattaa saamelaisten perinteiset elinkeinot kuten kalastuksen, poronhoidon, metsästyksen, keräilyn ja saamelaiskäsityön (duodji, tyeji, ǩiõtt-tuejj) sekä niiden nykyiset harjoittamisen muodot, luonnonvarojen kestävän hyödyntämisen sekä maan- ja vesien käytön. Lisäksi yhteistyötä tehdään saamelaismatkailun sekä aihepiireihin liittyvään yhteiskuntatieteelliseen tutkimukseen liittyvissä kysymyksissä.

- Luke haluaa tiivistää yhteistyötä Saamelaiskäräjien kanssa ja edistää luonnonvara-alan tutkimusta saamelaisten kotiseutualueella. Arktisen alueen tutkimuskysymykset ovat meille tärkeä strateginen ja kasvava painopiste. Saamelaisten kotiseutualueeseen liittyy monia luonnonvara-alalle tärkeitä tutkimuskysymyksiä ja olemme iloisia tästä sopimuksesta, kertoo pääjohtaja Johanna Buchert Luonnonvarakeskuksesta (Luke).

title: Culture as Democratic Infrastructure in a Changing Europe
content:
In Varietate Concordia — United in Diversity — captures one of Europe’s most enduring ambitions. Yet today, this principle is under increasing strain. Across the continent and beyond, societies are facing rising polarisation, declining trust in institutions, widening inequalities, rapid digital transformation, and the accelerating impacts of climate change. These pressures are not only political or economic — they are fundamentally relational. They shape how people perceive one another, how they interact, and how they imagine shared futures.

In this context, culture and heritage are often positioned as supportive or secondary policy domains. However, growing evidence suggests a different interpretation: culture and heritage function as critical democratic infrastructure. They shape the conditions under which democratic values are practiced, negotiated and sustained in everyday life (European Commission, 2023; Council of Europe, 2010). This article argues that culture should not be understood simply as a sector, but as an ecosystem of relationships and practices through which societies organise meaning, trust, identity and collective action.

title: “Evil Mickey Mouse” Invades Japan in a 1934 Japanese Anime Propaganda Film
content:
Before the Japanese fell completely, one hundred percent in love with anything and everything Disney (I mean, seriously, they love it), Mickey Mouse represented something completely different: Pure American imperialist evil.

At least he did in this 1934 animated propaganda cartoon Omochabako series dai san wa: Ehon senkya-hyakusanja-rokunen (Toybox Series 3: Picture Book 1936) by Komatsuzawa Hajime. It’s a convoluted title, but pretty simple in plot. An island of cute critters (including one Felix the Cat clone) is attacked from the air by an army of Mickey Mouses (Mickey Mice?) riding bats and assisted by crocodiles and snakes that act like machine guns. The frightened creatures call on the heroes of Japanese storybooks and folk legends to help them, from Momotaro (“Peach Boy”) and Kintaro (“Golden Boy”) to Issun-boshi (“One Inch Boy”) and Benkei, a warrior monk, to send Mickey packing. The not-so-subtle message: Mickey Mouse may be your hero, America, but our characters are older, more numerous, and way more beloved. Our pop culture is older than yours!

title: Armenia’s Relations With Russia? Worsening
content:
If you want one example of Armenia’s problems in shaking itself free of Russia’s influence, look at its rail system. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has repeatedly called for Russia to show flexibility and potentially transfer the concession to a third country acceptable to both sides. On 24 August, he again urged Russia to sell its concession rights to a mutually acceptable third party.

Russia has not answered, and it is unlikely to accept the idea. It has been running an escalating campaign to make life hard for Pashinyan, who was reelected in June. Putin makes no secret of this; indeed, he seems to delight in the (considerable) influence he can bring to bear.

That was clear at the September 1 meeting between the Russian and Armenian leaders at Bishkek, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. The reason is Armenia’s pursuit of closer ties with the European Union.

Putin sees this as a threat, as he once did with Ukraine. The EU’s anti-corruption, free trade, liberal democratic ethos is the antithesis of Russia’s approach.

title: Cold TAKE: Amazon's New Encryption Method Still Doesn't Deliver Real Privacy
content:
Amazon recently debuted a new feature for its Ring cameras that the company is calling Throw Away the Key Encryption (TAKE). The idea is to cut back on the amount of video content available to the company, and thus potentially available to law enforcement. But while it might technically add a speed bump to accessing full video content, it doesn’t deliver nearly the level of privacy we should be demanding from video doorbells and other security cameras.

TAKE introduces a new way for Ring to manage encryption keys, where the user’s device has its key, then the company holds encryption keys temporarily within its own cloud infrastructure. Ring’s servers receive the keys temporarily so it can offer a variety of the features it says it can’t offer when a user chooses to use end-to-end encryption, like video descriptions, smart alerts, video search, and more, then deletes the key after 24 hours. 

This differs from how it works now, where footage is encrypted in transit and at rest, then decrypted by Ring, which always has access to the footage, to process those features.
